tasks.title: Add the install/v1 schema, the install stamp's read and write, and semantic-version comparison
tasks.goal: Everything in this run that sets a repository up or checks it — init, upgrade, doctor — reads or writes the install stamp .vloop/install.json, so its contract lands first as the embedded schema install/v1 plus a small internal/install package that reads and writes it and compares versions. The comparison decides upgrade's whole behaviour table (equal, newer, breaking), so it is written and unit-tested here once, not re-derived by upgrade and doctor separately; it is gated end to end later by T7, which builds binaries at real versions. One pre-existing expectation must change, and changing it is required, not weakening: `schema list` gains install/v1 (and the embedded-schemas count in embed_test.go goes from 8 to 9).

references.why: 'The install stamp — .vloop/install.json, schema install/v1' (the exact document), 'vloop upgrade' (what 'breaking' means for 0.x and majors, pre-release versions needing --yes), and the Constraints item naming schema list as the one expectation that must change
the schema conventions install/v1 must follow: draft 2020-12, a `schema` property equal to the schema's own name, unknown keys allowed at every level, embedded and read only from the embedded FS
C-3: every JSON document vloop writes names its schema — the stamp is one

acceptance: `vloop schema list` prints exactly defect/v1, export/v1, install/v1, iteration/v1, metrics/v1, proposal/v1, session/v1, state/v1, verdict/v1, one per line. install/v1 lives in schemas/install.v1.json, is draft 2020-12, is embedded and read only from the embedded FS like the others, and has no `additionalProperties: false` or `unevaluatedProperties: false` anywhere.

install/v1 requires `schema` (const install/v1), `version` (string), `commit` (string), `initialized` (string) and `upgraded` (string or null — null until the first upgrade); the brief's example stamp validates.
internal/schema/testdata gains install.valid.json and install.invalid.json and the existing table-driven schema test covers them.

internal/install reads and writes .vloop/install.json (repo-relative constant, `/` separators, written through filepath on disk) and exposes the version comparison upgrade and doctor will share. Its committed tests cover: equal versions; from newer than to; numeric rather than textual comparison (0.1.9 < 0.1.10); breaking when majors differ, or when both majors are 0 and minors differ; not breaking for a 0.x patch or a same-major minor ≥1; and that any version with a pre-release suffix (0.0.0-dev) cannot be compared, so any upgrade to or from one is treated as needing --yes.
The comparison is implemented once in internal/install; no other package re-implements semver parsing. No third-party module is added for it without a reason in the task notes.

The only pre-existing test expectations changed are the schema list outputs (install/v1 added) in internal/schema, internal/cli and cmd/vloop, and the embedded-schema count in embed_test.go; no other assertion is removed or loosened.
No init, upgrade, doctor or plugin command appears in this task.

tasks.title: Fix F1: a binding reference's reason may wrap onto the lines indented under its list item
tasks.goal: `vloop brief check` reads only the first line of a `## Binding references` entry, so an entry whose reason starts on the next line — still one Markdown list item — is wrongly reported as having no reason (found writing this very brief). An entry becomes the whole list item: its first line plus every following line indented under it, up to the next item or heading; the reason is everything after the separator across those lines. The gate builds the base commit 05ea997 (the commit that added this brief) and proves the wrapped fixture fails there, so the fix is measured against the real defect.

references.why: 'F1 — a binding reference's reason may wrap': the definition of an entry (first line plus indented lines up to the next item or heading) and the gate's two fixtures

acceptance: An entry whose separator (` — ` or ` - `) ends its first line and whose reason is on the following indented line(s) passes `brief check` (`✓ binding references resolve and say why`); the same fixture fails against the base commit.
An entry with no reason on any of its lines — separator then a blank line or the next item, or no separator at all — still fails with `binding reference has no reason: <path>`.

A reason never carries over from one list item to the next: when a wrapped entry for x is followed by an entry for y with no reason, x passes and y is reported. A following line that is not indented is not part of the item.
One-line entries behave exactly as before, in English and Spanish briefs; the dead-reference and directory-entry-point checks still apply to wrapped entries.
internal/brief/refs_test.go gains tests whose names contain Wrap covering the wrapped pass, the no-reason-on-any-line failure and the next-item boundary.

tasks.title: Complete the plugin: valid manifests, the SessionStart hook, `vloop version --check-plugin` and `vloop plugin path`
tasks.goal: The plugin must become an installable marketplace entry (the marketplace has failed `claude plugin validate` since B1 for lack of `owner`), carry a SessionStart hook that warns when plugin and binary versions differ, and be extractable by the binary for B6's driver to pass with --plugin-dir. The hook is a Go command, not a script, so it works on Windows, and it must always exit 0 because a failing hook would interrupt every session. Sessions cannot run `claude`, so the real `claude plugin validate .` runs only in T10's gate; here the manifests are checked structurally. README.md is at B1's line cap (199 lines; the README test requires fewer than 200): documenting the new command and flags means tightening existing README text, never raising the cap or loosening the README test. docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated with `go generate ./...`, never hand-edited.

references.why: 'The plugin', 'vloop version --check-plugin <dir>' and 'vloop plugin path' — the exact messages, the always-exit-0 rule, idempotence and stray-file removal — and the security violations for check-plugin and plugin path
sections 2 and 6: how plugin and binary are tied (--plugin-dir, marketplace install, the mismatch hook) — the reason the hook exists and what plugin path is for
the embedded plugin (the all: embed prefix), its manifests, and how `vloop version` reports the embedded plugin version, which must keep working

acceptance: plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json gains a non-empty `description` and an `author` object with a `name`; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json gains `owner` with a `name` and a description, and still lists the vloop plugin at ./plugin. Nothing else about the manifests' names changes.

plugin/hooks/hooks.json declares exactly one hook, under SessionStart, of type command, whose command is exactly `vloop version --check-plugin "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"`. The embedded plugin includes it, and a Go test in plugin_embed_test.go (name containing Hook) asserts that.

`vloop version --check-plugin ` reads /.claude-plugin/plugin.json: equal versions print nothing; different versions print `vloop: the vloop plugin is

but the vloop binary is — update the one that is behind` on stdout; a missing, unreadable, non-JSON or version-less manifest prints `vloop: cannot read the vloop plugin's version in

` on stdout, with as given. It exits 0 in every one of these cases and writes nothing to stderr.
check-plugin only reads that one JSON file: it never executes, sources or evaluates anything from the plugin directory. Plain `vloop version` (and --json) is unchanged.

`vloop plugin path` extracts the embedded plugin into .vloop/tmp/plugin/<binary version>/ under the repo root (from any subdirectory) and prints that repo-relative path with `/`; --json prints {"path": "…"}. The extracted tree holds exactly the embedded files, byte for byte, except that the extracted .claude-plugin/plugin.json carries this binary's version as `version` (that is what makes the worked example's check-plugin on the extracted copy print nothing for the same binary).

plugin path is idempotent: files that already match are not rewritten (their modification times are untouched); a modified file is restored; files and directories the embedded plugin does not contain are removed from that version directory.
plugin path writes nothing outside .vloop/tmp/plugin/, and never follows a symlink out of the repository (a .vloop/tmp that is a symlink to an outside directory leaves that directory untouched).
README.md documents `vloop plugin path` and `--check-plugin` and stays under 200 lines; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated; B1's README test and the command-reference test pass unchanged.

tasks.title: Fix F2: stacks scoped by path — parse and validate `stack@path`, resolve scopes, match scope-relative, label scoped matches
tasks.goal: metrics.stacks is one repo-wide list and presets merge across the whole tree, so in a monorepo one stack's globs classify another's files (Python's **/tests/** makes web/tests/helpers.ts a test; C#'s **/bin/** excludes tools/bin/run.sh). An entry may now be `<stack>@<path>`; inside a scope only that scope's stacks apply, the longest scope wins, and a scoped preset matches paths relative to its scope's directory. This is a change to B3's classification (M-3's layers are otherwise unchanged) and init (T6) writes these scopes. The gate builds the base commit 05ea997 and shows the monorepo paths classify differently than the base code did, while unscoped stacks classify exactly as before.

references.why: 'F2 — stacks scoped by path': the entry syntax and its validation message, scope resolution, scope-relative matching, the classify label, and the monorepo fixture and output in the worked example
M-3: the layer order (always-excluded, the repo's own globs, then presets, else other) that scoping must leave intact
the Classification section: how layers and presets decide a path today, which scoped presets extend rather than replace

acceptance: An entry of metrics.stacks is `<stack>` or `<stack>@<path>`: a known stack, and a repo-relative path with `/`, no leading `/`, no trailing `/`, no `.` or `..` segment, naming an existing directory. `config set` rejects anything else with exit 2 and `vloop: invalid value "<entry>" for metrics.stacks: want <stack> or <stack>@<existing directory>` naming the offending entry — for a missing directory exactly as the brief shows — and leaves the config file untouched.

Reading the config checks an entry's form but not the directory's existence: a scope whose directory has since vanished is still a readable config (doctor warns about it in T8), while a malformed entry in the file is a config problem (exit 1).
A path's scope is the longest scoped path that contains it; with none, the unscoped stacks apply. Inside a scope only that scope's stacks apply — unscoped stacks do not add to them.

A scoped preset's globs are matched against the path relative to the scope's directory (services/api/Api.Tests/CalcTests.cs is tested as Api.Tests/CalcTests.cs; services/x/go.sum against go.sum). The repo's own globs stay repo-relative and unscoped; always-excluded comes first; the layer order is otherwise unchanged.
`metrics classify` labels a scoped match `(<stack>@<path>: <glob>)`; an unscoped match keeps `(<stack>: <glob>)`. The brief's monorepo classification lines match exactly.

With the same stacks written unscoped, classification is identical to the base code's; the scoped config classifies web/tests/helpers.ts and tools/bin/run.sh differently. Every existing classify, metrics and B3 end-to-end test passes unchanged.

Committed tests whose names contain Scope in internal/classify and internal/config cover parsing and validation, longest-scope resolution, scope-relative matching and the label. Nothing assumes `/` on disk: scope directories are checked through filepath.

tasks.title: Detect stacks per directory: the marker table, the C# solution rule, skipped directories, sorted scoped output
tasks.goal: init (T6) writes metrics.stacks from what it finds, so detection is its own unit: walk the repo root and directories up to three levels below it, treat a directory holding a marker file as a stack root, and return the entries init writes — unscoped for the root, `<stack>@<dir>` below it — sorted unscoped first. The gate exercises it through the pinned function detect.Stacks(root string) ([]string, error) in package internal/detect, with one fixture per rule where it applies and where it must not.

references.why: 'Stack detection' under vloop init: the marker table, the C# solution rule, the skipped directories, the three-level depth and the sorted, unscoped-first output

acceptance: Package internal/detect exports `Stacks(root string) ([]string, error)` returning the entries init will write: stacks found at the root unscoped, stacks found in a subdirectory as `<stack>@<dir>` with `/`; unscoped entries first, each group sorted; an empty result when nothing is found.

Markers: go.mod → go; package.json → javascript, plus typescript when a tsconfig.json sits beside it or typescript is a dependency (dependencies or devDependencies), plus react when react is a dependency (a mention of react anywhere else in package.json does not count); *.csproj or *.sln → csharp; pyproject.toml, requirements.txt or setup.py → python; pom.xml or build.gradle → java; build.gradle.kts → kotlin (not java); Cargo.toml → rust. A tsconfig.json alone is not a marker.

For C#, the stack root is the directory of a *.sln at or above the *.csproj files if there is one, else each *.csproj's own directory; one solution yields one entry however many projects sit under it.

The walk covers the root and directories up to three levels below it (a/b/c yes, a/b/c/d no) and skips directories named .git, .vloop, .loop, node_modules, vendor, bin, obj, dist, target and build at any depth.
Detection only reads: it never writes, never follows a symlink out of the repository, and does not assume a case-sensitive filesystem or `/` on disk.
internal/detect/detect_test.go covers each marker rule where it applies and where it must not, the solution rule, the skipped directories, the depth limit and the ordering.

tasks.title: Add `vloop init`: config with detected stacks, the stamp, a starter brief, the .gitignore line and the CLAUDE.md section
tasks.goal: `vloop init` is how a consumer repository gets set up: it writes .vloop/config.toml (language and detected or given stacks), the install stamp, a starter brief exactly as `vloop brief new` writes it, the .vloop/tmp/ line in .gitignore, and vloop's section in CLAUDE.md between `<!-- vloop:begin -->` and `<!-- vloop:end -->` — and nothing else. It refuses a repository vloop already set up (only upgrade changes one), keeps what the operator already has byte for byte, never commits, and never touches .claude/settings.json or .loop/. The CLAUDE.md section and .gitignore line are what T7's upgrade refreshes, so write them where upgrade can reuse them; the section names the vloop version that wrote it. README.md is at B1's line cap (199 lines; the README test requires fewer than 200): documenting the new command and flags means tightening existing README text, never raising the cap or loosening the README test. docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated with `go generate ./...`.

references.why: 'vloop init': the refusal table and messages, the five writes and their print lines, the next-steps block, --dry-run, and the worked example's init lines and planted failures; 'Violations the review must rule on'
the precedent init ports: the CLAUDE.md section between markers (replace between, append when absent), the .gitignore line appended once, the version stamp, never .claude/settings.json
C-1 and C-2: config is repo-local and the repo root is the nearest ancestor holding .vloop, else .git — init must write under that root
the configuration keys (language, metrics.stacks) init writes and the CLI conventions its output follows

acceptance: Refusals, each writing nothing, --dry-run included: no .git at the repo root → `vloop: not a git repository — run git init first`, exit 1; .vloop/install.json exists → `vloop: already initialized by vloop <version> — run vloop upgrade`, exit 1; an invalid --language or stack (including a scope naming a missing directory) → B1's invalid-value message, exit 2.

The worked example's `vloop init --language es` prints exactly: `detected stacks: go, javascript, react`, `wrote .vloop/config.toml`, `wrote .vloop/install.json`, `wrote docs/briefs/B<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>-primeros-pasos.loop-brief.md`, `updated .gitignore`, `wrote CLAUDE.md`, then the three-line `next:` block, exit 0. A created .gitignore prints `wrote .gitignore`; `detected stacks: none` when nothing is found.

.vloop/config.toml gets `language` (default en) and metrics.stacks (--stacks as given, else detected). An existing config file is kept byte for byte (`kept .vloop/config.toml`) and init proceeds; detected stacks it lacks are printed as a suggestion, not written.
.vloop/install.json validates against install/v1 with this binary's version and commit, `initialized` as a UTC timestamp and `upgraded` null.

The starter brief is byte-for-byte what `vloop brief new getting-started` (en) or `primeros-pasos` (es) writes, status: draft. When docs/briefs/ already holds a *.loop-brief.md it is skipped (`kept docs/briefs/`); other files there do not count.
.gitignore gains the line .vloop/tmp/ once, on its own line even when the file lacked a final newline; nothing else in it changes. It is created if absent.

tasks.goal: Once a repository is set up, only `vloop upgrade` changes it, and deliberately: it compares the stamp's version with this binary's using T1's comparison, refuses a downgrade outright and a breaking jump without --yes (showing what it would change first), and otherwise refreshes exactly the vloop-owned parts — the CLAUDE.md section between its markers and the .gitignore line — then rewrites the stamp. It never touches config values, briefs, plans, defects or interventions. Only built binaries at different versions show this, so the gate builds eight. README.md is at B1's line cap (199 lines; the README test requires fewer than 200): documenting the new command and flags means tightening existing README text, never raising the cap or loosening the README test. docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated with `go generate ./...`.

references.why: 'vloop upgrade': the behaviour table and its messages, 'breaking' for 0.x and majors, pre-release versions, the exact set of changes, --dry-run; and the worked example's upgrade lines
the marker-replacement precedent: only the text between the markers changes, the operator's own text is kept

acceptance: No stamp → `vloop: not initialized — run vloop init`, exit 1. from = to → `already at <to>`, exit 0, nothing written.

from > to → `vloop: this repository was set up by vloop <from>, newer than this binary (<to>) — upgrade the binary, not the repository`, exit 1, nothing written, with or without --yes. Versions compare numerically (0.1.10 is newer than 0.1.9).

A breaking jump (majors differ, or both majors 0 and minors differ) without --yes prints the changes it would make (`would update <path>` lines) and then `vloop: <from> → <to> may break this repository's setup — review the changes above, then run vloop upgrade --yes` on stderr, exit 1, nothing written. Any upgrade to or from a pre-release version (0.0.0-dev) is treated the same way.

Otherwise, or with --yes, it applies the changes, prints `updated <path>` for each path whose content changed (the worked example: `updated CLAUDE.md` then `updated .vloop/install.json`), and rewrites the stamp's version, commit and upgraded (UTC timestamp), keeping initialized.

The changes are exactly vloop's CLAUDE.md section (between the markers; the operator's text above and below is byte-identical afterwards) and the .gitignore line (re-added if removed; the file otherwise unchanged). Because the section names the version that wrote it, an upgrade across versions updates it.
upgrade never touches config values, briefs, plans, defects, interventions, .claude/ or .loop/, never commits, and never follows a symlink out of the repository when writing.
--dry-run prints `would update <path>` for each change and writes nothing.

README.md documents `vloop upgrade` with --yes and --dry-run and stays under 200 lines; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated. Committed tests whose names contain Upgrade cover every row of the table, marker-only changes and --dry-run.

tasks.title: Add `vloop doctor`: git, install, config, claude, trust, gate shell, plan, branch, plugin, stacks and self-hosting checks
tasks.goal: `vloop doctor` says whether a repository, the toolchain and the plugin are ready for a run, porting the shell loop's preflight (tools on PATH, workspace trust, git identity, a valid plan) and adding the install, plugin-version, scoped-stack and self-hosting checks. It reads only: it writes nothing and runs nothing but git, `claude --version`, `claude plugin list --json` and PATH lookups; reading the user's Claude settings for trust is the one place it looks outside the repository. Tests use a stub `claude` on PATH and a fake home — sessions cannot run the real one. README.md is at B1's line cap (199 lines; the README test requires fewer than 200): documenting the new command and flags means tightening existing README text, never raising the cap or loosening the README test. docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated with `go generate ./...`.

references.why: 'vloop doctor': the check table (what is a problem, what a warning), the output and --json shapes, what doctor may run; the worked example's doctor output and planted failures
preflight: the checks doctor ports — tools on PATH, workspace trust read from $HOME/.claude.json `.projects[<repo path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted`, git identity, a valid plan
R-2 (a run happens on a work branch, never the default branch) behind the branch check, and S-2

acceptance: Text output is one line per check — `✓` pass, `!` warning, `✗` problem, `-` not applicable — then `doctor: <n> problem(s), <m> warning(s)`; exit 1 if any problem, else 0. The worked example prints exactly ✓ git, ✓ install, ✓ config, ✓ claude, ✓ trust, ✓ gate shell, - plan, - branch, ✓ plugin, - self-hosting and `doctor: 0 problem(s), 0 warning(s)`. A pass line is the symbol and the name; a warning or problem line adds its message after the name.

--json prints {"ok":bool,"checks":[{"name","result":"pass|warning|problem|n/a","message"}]}, checks in the order git, install, config, claude, trust, gate shell, plan, branch, plugin, stacks, self-hosting. The stacks check appears only when metrics.stacks holds a scoped entry (the worked example has none and shows no stacks line).

git: problem when not a git repository or user.name/user.email is unset. install: warning when not initialized or the stamp is older (message says `run vloop upgrade`); problem when the stamp is newer than the binary. config: problem when .vloop/config.toml does not parse or holds an invalid value. claude: problem when `claude` is not on PATH.

trust: warning when $HOME/.claude.json does not mark this repository's root trusted (`.projects[<root>].hasTrustDialogAccepted`), message including `run claude here once and accept the trust dialog`; a missing or unreadable file is the same warning, never a problem.

gate shell: with a plan (.vloop/state/state.json), problem when its `shell` is not on PATH; without one, warning when the configured shell is not on PATH. plan: problem when a plan exists and fails `task validate`; n/a without one. branch: problem when a plan is running or planning and HEAD is on the default branch (R-2); n/a without a plan.

plugin: warning when `claude plugin list --json` shows no enabled plugin whose id is `vloop@<any marketplace>`, or its version differs from this binary's. The gate's stub prints a JSON array of {"id","version","scope","enabled"} objects.

stacks: warning `<stack>@<path>: no such directory` for each scoped entry whose directory no longer exists. self-hosting: warning when the repository is vloop's own (go.mod declares module github.com/mvelosop/vloop) and the binary's commit stamp is HEAD (a short stamp matches as a prefix of HEAD's sha).
doctor writes nothing anywhere, and runs no command other than git, `claude --version`, `claude plugin list --json` and PATH lookups.

README.md documents `vloop doctor` and stays under 200 lines; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated. Committed tests whose names contain Doctor, using a stub claude and a fake home, cover every check in each of its results.

The command reference is generated, never hand-edited, and B1's README test must pass with every new command in the README. Nothing from B6 (run, the skills) is described as if it exists.

references.why: Shape item 8 (which documents gain what) and the behaviour contract the docs must describe as built
what B5 owns and what B6/B7 own — the docs must not describe B6's run or skills as built
the configuration keys and the schemas list — the configuration guide's account of metrics.stacks and install/v1 must agree with it

acceptance: README.md documents vloop init, vloop upgrade, vloop doctor, vloop plugin path and --check-plugin with their flags, stays under 200 lines, and B1's README test passes unchanged.
docs/guide/commands.md is exactly what `go generate ./...` produces (TestCommandsReferenceIsCurrent passes).
docs/guide/configuration.md documents .vloop/install.json and install/v1, the `<stack>@<path>` form with an example such as csharp@services/api, the longest-scope rule and the .vloop/tmp/ line.
docs/guide/metrics.md's Line classification section explains scopes: only a scope's stacks apply inside it, globs match relative to the scope's directory, and the `(<stack>@<path>: <glob>)` label.

docs/guide/concepts.md gains a 'Setting up a repository' section covering init (what it writes, the .gitignore line and CLAUDE.md section, the stamp), upgrade and --yes, doctor, and the marketplace install next steps.
docs/domain/domain-model.md's M-3 and docs/domain/measurement/metrics.md's Classification section state scopes (longest scope wins, only that scope's stacks, the `@` syntax) as built.
internal/cli/guide_test.go gains checks that the configuration guide covers the stamp and scoped stacks, so the docs cannot silently drift from the code.
No absolute paths; nothing describes `vloop run`, the /vloop: skills or the B7 review as existing.

tasks.title: Close: the end-to-end B5 worked example, the real-data check and `claude plugin validate .`
tasks.goal: Unit tests on fixtures can pass while built binaries misbehave: only binaries built at 0.1.0, 0.1.1 and 0.2.0 show upgrade's refusals, and only the real `claude` shows the marketplace is valid. This task commits cmd/vloop/b5_e2e_test.go, which builds the binaries with -ldflags -X and plays the brief's worked example line for line — with a stub claude and a fake home — plus the monorepo and every planted failure. Its gate also runs the real-data check on this repository, read-only, and the real `claude plugin validate .`, which sessions cannot run.

references.why: 'Worked example' (every command, output line and planted failure the end-to-end test plays, the monorepo fixture) and 'Real data'
the package's TestMain and scratch-repository harness the B5 tests reuse rather than copy

acceptance: cmd/vloop/b5_e2e_test.go holds TestWorkedExampleB5… tests that build vloop at 0.1.0, 0.1.1 and 0.2.0 with -ldflags -X and play the worked example line for line in t.TempDir() fixtures, addressed with git -C: init --language es (every line), config get, the second init, doctor with the stub reporting vloop@vloop 0.1.0, the three upgrades and the older-binary refusal, plugin path, and check-plugin at both versions.

The same file plays the monorepo (init's detected stacks line, the six classify lines, the rejected config set) and every planted failure: no .git, operator text around existing markers then upgrade (byte for byte), an existing config kept, docs/briefs/ already holding a brief, the plugin-version warning, no user.email, a non-JSON plugin.json, and a stray file removed by plugin path.

The stub claude is a script the test writes into a temporary directory placed first on PATH; the fake home carries .claude.json marking the fixture trusted. No test reads or writes this repository's .loop/, .claude/, .vloop/, git history or the real home directory.

Real data (this gate only, read-only): `vloop init --dry-run` on this repository prints `detected stacks: go` and `would keep .vloop/config.toml`; `vloop doctor` exits 0 with `! install`; `claude plugin validate .` passes with no errors and no warnings; this repository's git status is unchanged afterwards.
`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `go mod tidy -diff` and the linux, windows and host builds are all clean.
No B6 or B7 work appears anywhere in the run: no skills under plugin/skills/, no `run`, no fence as embedded data, no whole-package review; this repository is not initialised by vloop.
